Hex-Rays typed them `double (*)(void)` (a cast, data/callsite_args.json src=cast), so the reconstruction called the method with whatever ECX held. Slot 12 of every timer vtable (CXiTimer 0x1032A0B0, CXiTimerHigh 0x1032A0C4, CXiTimerLow 0x1032A118) is CXiTimer::GetFps 0x10019230, `fld dword ptr [ecx+8]; ret`, which reads ECX (data/ecx_use.json). The call is __thiscall with the timer, as the next call (+36) already is. Both are declared __thiscall in data/type_fixes.json and called with the object the original passes. The call to CXiMovie_DrawFrame (0x1021D4C0) passes five stack arguments the IDB's type (int __cdecl()) leaves out: 0x10012A46..0x10012A77 push &SystemTime (four floats Hex-Rays stored into the reused SYSTEMTIME slot: 0, width*0.0015625, -110 or -160, height*0.0021453374) and write the rectangle {0, EBX = 0, 0x280, 0x200} below it. They are passed as the original does. -- After each call of exit_0 (0x100182E0) the original goes on to LABEL_102 (0x100121C4: `mov eax,[0x1045666C]; mov [eax+0x828], bl`): the four sites 0x10011BFA (4003), 0x10011C1E (4004), 0x10011C37 (4005) and 0x10011C62 (2001) are each followed by `add esp, 4; jmp 0x100121C4`. The IDB marks exit_0 as not returning, so Hex-Rays dropped those jumps (4003 fell into case 203, 2001 into LABEL_38). exit_0 does return: it calls 0x10018310, which returns at once when the byte at 0x10350E38 is 0 (0x10018316 `test al, al; je 0x10018348` -> `pop esi; ret`).
